On this CR52 the no-flush pass does not reproduce the hazard for
CPU-vs-CPU access (the core hazard-checks non-cacheable reads
against L1D) -- recorded as a finding. A real DMA master is a
separate observer; the flush-first pass stays the rule.
Cortex-A55 has no choice 3/4: it is not one of the bus masters the
Address Expander serves, so this two-window aliasing this demo
depends on does not exist on that core (see end-of-diagram note).
[direction in the 4 memcpy directions (cached/non-cached DDR, DDR<->SYSTEM_RAM)]
ddr_ep_cyc_read() -> elapsed cycles -> us via SystemCoreClock
The ARM generic timer's CNTFRQ reads 0 on this core, so the
PMU cycle counter is used. This is a scalar-memcpy cached-vs-
non-cached ratio check, not a controller bandwidth figure.
